root.name: English Defense: Poli Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 e6 2. c4 b6 3. e4 Bb7 4. f3 f5 5. exf5 Nh6

overview: White builds a big centre with 3.e4 and 4.f3, and Black strikes at once with ...f5 and 5...Nh6, offering the f-pawn for quick development and pressure on the centre. White can take on f5 and hold material, then must catch up in development without being hit by ...Bb4+ or ...Qh4+ checks on the weakened kingside. The play is double-edged and rare.

white_ideas.idea: Take f5, keep the extra pawn and consolidate with Nc3, Bd3, Ne2.
Use the big e4-d4-c4 centre once Black's pieces have been dislodged.

black_ideas.idea: Win time with ...Nxf5, ...Bb4+ and ...Qh4+ against the weakened e1-h4 diagonal.
Undermine the centre with ...Bb7 and ...c5 or ...d5.

typical_structures.structure: White d4/c4/f3 centre against Black pieces aimed at it from b7, h6 and the b4/h4 diagonals.

character.notes: Both sides run risks: White has loosened his king with f3 while Black is a pawn down for time.

gambit.notes: Black gives up the f5 pawn after 5.exf5 for development and attacking chances, and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: A gambit that gives up a pawn for development against a solid centre; strong players tend to rate White's extra pawn.

structure.notes: Central pawns trade off on e4 and f5, leaving an asymmetric semi-open centre with Black pieces eyeing d4 and e4.

approach.notes: Rarely seen even among English Defence players; chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Tactical but short; dubious lines are never Beginner.
